gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 4?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Current ensemble runs show daytime maxima reaching the mid-30s Celsius under mostly sunny conditions and light winds, with limited cloud cover or precipitation expected to suppress peaks. This aligns with observed regional heat trends through early August, where official measurements have already approached similar thresholds. Model spread remains modest but acknowledges typical uncertainties in boundary-layer heating and local urban effects that could shift the exact maximum by 1–2°C. Updated runs ahead of resolution will refine these implied probabilities as new observational data arrives.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for London's highest temperature on August 4, 2026, centers on 28–30°C as the dominant range, with 29°C holding the highest implied probability at 48.5%.** This positioning reflects ensemble forecast guidance from the Met Office and ECMWF, which indicate a continuation of above-average warmth driven by southerly flow of subtropical air and residual high-pressure influence across southern England. August climatology places London's typical daily maximum near 22–23°C, so current model consensus represents a +6–7°C anomaly consistent with the broader 2026 summer pattern of repeated heat episodes.

Urban heat-island effects in central London stations, combined with light winds and partial cloud cover, support peak readings in this band. Recent model runs have shown limited spread, keeping 31°C+ probabilities low while assigning minimal weight to 27°C or below. As the day progresses, real-time observations from Heathrow, Kew, and Northolt—updated hourly by the Met Office—will determine the exact maximum and drive any final repricing before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Tokyo's early August temperatures are shaped by the strengthening Pacific subtropical high, which promotes subsidence, clear skies, and above-normal heat following the end of the Baiu rainy season. Japan Meteorological Agency seasonal outlooks issued in late July project warmer-than-average conditions nationwide through August 2026, consistent with the preceding record-hot summer. Short-range guidance for August 6 indicates a daytime high near 32–33 °C under partly cloudy skies with possible showers, typical of urban heat-island amplification in the Tokyo basin where concrete and limited ventilation add 1–2 °C. Model consensus clusters tightly around these values, with modest uncertainty from afternoon convection or slight shifts in steering flow; historical August maxima average 31–32 °C, placing the market-implied distribution squarely within climatological norms.
